title: Detecting TLS Certificate and User-Agent Anomalies

content_blocks.content: Operating systems are where security gets physical. Forget the marketing — the guts decide what's actually possible.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.content: These lessons cover how Windows, Linux, and related subsystems manage processes, permissions, services, and trust.

content_blocks.title: Teach Me Like I'm 10: The Building Manager
content_blocks.content: The OS is the building manager. Processes are tenants, permissions are keys, services are scheduled workers, and the kernel is the security guard nobody argues with.

content_blocks.title: Quick inspection habit
content_blocks.content: Look at the running process, its parent, its permissions, and what starts it. Weirdness usually hides there.

content_blocks.title: Why it matters
content_blocks.content: Attackers abuse normal system features because normal features are trusted. That's why internals matter.

content_blocks.title: System internals cue
content_blocks.content: Process, thread, token, service, ACL, driver, trust chain.

content_blocks.title: Think it through
content_blocks.content: Which control would you harden first on a real workstation: services, ACLs, or scripting?
If the OS feels abstract, you're not done yet. Security lives in the details.
